text:
alex: Heads-up — observed a massive billing/ingest spike this AM driven by one trace_id (huge fanout). Dumping the tail counts now, but we should treat this as a hot-key problem not a user bug. :boom:

morgan: Ugh. Is it a single tenant or a single request id? can you paste the top few traces?

alex: single trace_id across many events; looks like a flaky client retry loop emitting identical spans. top: trace=abcd-ef01 repeated ~120k events in 6m.

tara: This is the classic hot-key / billing anchor. Options: 1) upstream rate-limit per-tenant/trace, 2) probabilistic downsample on ingest for dominant keys, 3) detect & bubble to support + block, 4) perform local de-dup by fingerprinting. Tradeoffs: correctness vs accounting fidelity.

ryan: Agree. Minimal-risk quick fix: deterministic probabilistic sampler keyed by trace_id where sample_rate = f(trace_freq_rank). That keeps stats reproducible.

alex: Example heuristic I sketched: if a single key > 0.5% of window events, start applying a floor sample rate = max(1/(1 + freq/threshold), min_rate). Also emit a metric (hot_trace_shares) so billing can backfill.

morgan: Would prefer explicit cap per-trace emission for billing accounting. E.g. "cap_events_per_minute" so even if a client misbehaves we don't blow quota.

tara: Caps are simpler to reason about but are brittle for bursts. Prob-sample + cap seems safe. Implementation idea: two-stage middleware in ingestion router: (1) detect top-N hot keys every 60s, (2) attach policy for those keys (prob-sample + hard cap).

ryan: Pseudo-config:```yaml
ingest.hot_key_detector:
  window_seconds: 60
  top_n: 100
  threshold_pct: 0.5
ingest.policies:
  - name: hot_key_shepherd
    action:
      type: probabilistic
      min_rate: 0.01
      max_reduction: 1000
    hard_cap_per_minute: 1000
```

alex: We also need to ensure billing doesn't silently drop events — add an "inferred_drop" tag that marks probabilistically-sampled events, and record counts pre/post so revenue/cost reconciliation can adjust.

morgan: Important: make the sampling deterministic for a given trace_id+seed so replaying logs / analytics yields the same subset. Use `hash(trace_id) % 10000 < (rate*10000)` pattern.

tara: We'll need metrics: hot_key_detected{shard,trace_family}, hot_key_precap_count, hot_key_postcap_count, hot_key_dropped_estimate. Also an alert when a single key > 1% for > 2 windows.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout queued for feature/hot-key-guard v0.1 -> staging at 12:30 UTC.

ryan: For long-term, consider moving fingerprinting earlier in the edge proxy to prevent shard amplification (consistent-hash + per-proxy reservoir). That reduces cross-shard coordination.

alex: Implementation plan proposal: 1) ship detector/metrics + deterministic prob-sample in ingest router (owner: ryan, ETA 2w), 2) add hard-cap config and alerting (owner: tara, ETA 1w), 3) patch billing backfill tooling to annotate dropped counts (owner: morgan, ETA 3w).

morgan: ok to create an RFC PR with config knobs and test harness? I'll wire a small replay dataset to validate cost reconcilation.

tara: +1. Also add a developer-facing FAQ: "why did my trace get capped?" and provide lookup by trace_id.

alex: Cool. I'll file the follow-ups and link them here. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
